sourceOccurrences.label: Left continuity and vanishing boundary flux
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: Left continuity allows infinite susceptibility and needs no summable-row assumption. Vanishing boundary flux needs finite susceptibility at one root and a finite uniform probability-row bound, but no transitivity. The three-way RDF0 equivalence is not exported here.

sourceOccurrences.label: Transitive contraction and critical boundary flux
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: Finite-row continuity, transport, persistence of a contracting set and R84Z are exported. Source automorphisms preserve all unordered-pair weights; diagonal erasure gives the graph interpretation with off-diagonal invariance. The full threshold identification and density theorem are separate.

sourceOccurrences.label: Integration and exhaustion for supercritical density
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: These are integration lemmas and conditional percolation consequences. The finite-volume escape differential inequality remains an explicit hypothesis; this file does not supply it or identify the finite-size threshold with the percolation threshold.

sourceOccurrences.label: The unexplored region and internal independence
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: The event specifying the unexplored region is unaffected by internal coordinates. The product-law factorization is an identity of event probabilities, including null events; it supplies the first part of HATE.

sourceOccurrences.label: The finite-domain escape derivative
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: The source supplies the exact derivative and finite-size differential inequality in HATE, with summable rows and no transitivity. The derivative at zero is from the right. The Train 7 appendix evaluates the two-vertex escape probability and derivative; it does not identify the global threshold.

proofUses.reason: The proof factorises P(S=T, o<->_T u) by independence, identifies closed pivotal bonds, and applies the finite intensity Russo formula (IENL).
Below t the finite-size susceptibility criterion (YLZV) gives finite susceptibility; above t the differential inequality of HATE is integrated and the domains are exhausted.
Contraction implies finite susceptibility by YLZV and the threshold theorem L0TE; the converse uses dominated convergence and the persistence argument of the critical-flux theorem (R84Z).
